customer_updates.text: Sunsets & regular scenes at Gorai Jetty.

featured_reviews.name: Shrut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have visited Gorai Khadi many times with my family and friends, and every time it feels peaceful and refreshing. It is a beautiful hidden place in Mumbai where you can enjoy calm water, fresh air, and nature. Sometimes you can also spot migratory birds, which makes the experience even more special.
The best part is that it is completely free to visit, so anyone can come and relax without spending money. From here, you can also ferry travel towards Gorai Beach, Pagoda, and Water Kingdom, soon open Gorai Mangrove Park
गोराई मैंग्रोव पार्क
this reason which makes it a convenient location.
A very nice place to spend quiet time away from the city crowd.
Avoid weekend because it's to much crowded.
♿ ✅
🚮✅
🚻✅
🅿️❌ You can search Road side free parking

featured_reviews.name: Kshitij Srivastava
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gorai Jetty is used mainly for two destinations. One is Essel World and Pagoda and another is to Gorai area. The jetty has undergone recent upgrades, making it safer and more accessible for passengers. The improvements include a wider and leveled platform, which is no longer prone to flooding during high tides.

The ferry ride from Gorai Jetty to Essel World or other nearby destinations is a great way to experience the beautiful surroundings.

Ferry is every 15-20 minutes. The last ferry departs from Pagoda side at 06:00 P.M.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Pisat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gorai Jetty is a convenient and scenic gateway to Gorai. The ferry ride is quick, affordable, and offers beautiful views of the creek, especially during sunset. The atmosphere is peaceful and makes the journey enjoyable.
A great place to enjoy a short ferry ride and experience a different side of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Karan Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: Its good place u have to take ferry to go there fees is free only 200 for return farry ticket. U can get food there in canteen its affordable.  U r not allowed to carry ur own food . There is good security at place. Kind and soothing place.

featured_reviews.name: Sou L
featured_reviews.review_text: Gorai Jetty is the starting point of a calm and scenic ferry ride 🌊⛴️ Surrounded by peaceful water views and fresh breeze, it gives a mini travel vibe even before you reach Gorai Beach or the Pagoda. The short ferry ride is smooth, affordable, and a fun experience perfect for a quick escape from the city hustle.

featured_reviews.name: ujjal dey
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gorai Jetty is the main access point to catch boats for Gorai Beach. The jetty is generally clean and well-maintained, making the ferry experience convenient and orderly. Over the past few years, however, there appears to be a noticeable reduction in water depth near the jetty, and some dredging work is currently in progress to address this.
Its location is a plus—it’s close to the upcoming Borivali Mangrove Trail, adding to the area’s appeal. Accessibility is good, with an auto stand and bus stand right next to the jetty, making it easy to reach for daily commuters as well as beachgoers.

featured_reviews.name: Sameer Pimpale
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is MAD busy, like, always-on-the-go crazy! 😅 You'll rub shoulders with fisherwomen, office workers, kids, families, and lovestruck couples, all on a mission. But don't worry, the boat service is on point – super efficient! The crew's got your back, too – they're helpful and know what's what. Get here early, and you can snag some fresh fish at a steal. And if you can tune out the chaos (big if, I know 🤯), you'll catch some stunning views – sunset is the magic hour, obvious 🌅.

featured_reviews.name: Suhas Shahane
featured_reviews.review_text: Take the quick and convenient ferry to Water Kingdom! The ride is under 10 minutes and only costs ₹15 per ticket. Alternatively, you can drive your personal vehicle (car/bike) to the drop-off point on the far end.

featured_reviews.name: vaibhav khedekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Although u will get fresh fish in this market its best to avoid going to this place considering its filthy condition and ridiculous crowd especially now during the pandemic situation. Also, the prices of fish is way too high compared to the quality and variety they have to offer. So only come here if u have no other choice really.
On the othee hand, u can always buys good quality meat here at really competitive prices and very kind and polite shopkeepers. A big thumbs up for the service they provide and the way they cater to ur needs is just fantastic ..
All in all a BIG "NO NO" for the fish market but definitely a "GO" for chicken and goat meat of the best quality and freshness.
Cheers foodies !!!

featured_reviews.review_text: This is a nice place for fish/prawns buying. Market starts at 7 AM. You have to be tough negotiator here. Do not be in rush to buy, there are plenty of options, be careful while buying, there are chances you may be robbed of old fishes. featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent for fresh sea food and sea food lovers who like cooking. A wide variety of fresh catch is available with fish like Pomphrets, Prawns / Shrimps, Crabs, lobsters et al.
The fresh catch comes every alternate day from the aversive jetty where the trawlers arrive every alternate days or so.

featured_reviews.name: asif sharief shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: Very good place for holesale fish in all variety

featured_reviews.name: Salim Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: Fish market at Andheri west Versova. You need to have good bargain skills to buy anything from here. The sellers are quite humble and polite,  but also be ready to get insulted if you are trying to bargain at a very low price below the expected lowest price and when you irritate them. Don't get emotionally carried away with the stories the sellers might try to sell. They will never sell even at their cost price. And the term 'bony karo' will be heard a lot. Don't get carried away. They will never give away unless they make profits. Generally the fishes are quite fresh and good to eat. The quantity matters for a good deal.

featured_reviews.name: Manish Dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a good place if you need to buy fish in large quantities. You will find fresh & good quality of Prawns, Surmai, Pomfret, Bangda & Bombayduck. Make sure to be there between 8AM to 9:30AM. Because after this time it is the small retailers who sell there. And if you want to get the fish cleaned : de-shelling the prawns, cleaning Bombayduck etc. you can get it done from small errand boys and girls who will do it for 30-50 Rs. Also be prepared to dare thru some fish slurry on the floor and ofcourse the STRONG  stench of fish.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Used to be one of the very well maintained joggers track till about 2019 however the park is not being maintained now.
You can see a lot of debris and construction materials lying around.
The park is still used by local for jogging, walking and relaxation by senior citizens.
It is still amongst the good tracks for fitness enthusiast in this area.
Pond is the major attraction at the joggers park, making the the walk/run worthwhile. You can also see a lot of kids and families feeding fishes, turtles and ducks in the pond.
You do have place to sit around the pond incase you just want to enjoy your time with family and friends.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Good food, quite authentic in taste. We had prawn manchow soup which was loaded with prawns. Their prawn lollypops are great, we also had squid tawa masala which was a bit salty but well cooked. We ordered thalis which was the main aim. Surmai and pomfret. The size was very good and fish was fresh. The thali was very good - rice, bhakri ( u can choose amboli or even chapati) , bhurji, sukka, prawn curry, bangda curry, salad and ofcourse rawa fry of the fish you choose. The place is very tiny with only 8 tables but service is prompt and nice ambience for a homely meal
.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

The staffs are good, polite and helpful. It's a small restaurant not apt to take your pet as pets do not have place to move around there.

featured_reviews.name: Dr.Ajinkya Dhekne
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited here for lunch yesterday.  Initially it was empty, then got full. Good food. We had oredered Pomfret Thali & Goan Chicken Thali. I tasted both, for me fish 🐟 is ordinary, chicken was good, especially chiken cafreal was tasty 😋.  A suggestion to owners : Dont include chicken lollypop in a thali, you can hive chiken tawa fry in your goa special spices like rechado & so on. Please balance your fish thali, for me everything was bit too sour - tangy. A good balance in tatste would be better idea, but hey that's just my opinion. A slightly expensive but I dont mind if you justify it with food which up to certain limit you do, but you fall short in service, start providing finger bowls that would be nice & expected given your price point.  Best of luck 👍
